summary.intent: Respond to the Track 3 Buildathon 'Noon Curveball' constraint, which invalidated the assumption that git diff is the sole record of agent changes, by adding agent session transcript parsing as a second evidence source to entire-guard.
summary.outcome: Designed and implemented a full session transcript subsystem (src/evidence/session/) supporting two transcript formats, with claim reconciliation, safety invariants, and 82 passing tests (33 pre-existing + 49 new); committed 32 files and triggered an Entire checkpoint.

repo: DESIGN.md is gitignored — it is a local planning document, not part of the deliverable; submission narrative goes in BUILDATHON.md and evidence/ instead
Entire titles checkpoints from the active user prompt, not commit messages — link checkpoints by ID in submissions, not by title
The graph impact runs must be captured BEFORE any edit; the card explicitly scores graph use after implementation in the partial band only
adjudicate() had 5 direct callers, 3 of which were test files — all new fields had to be additive/optional so no pre-existing test required modification
changedSince's only caller is core.ts:106 inside verify — the git adapter needed no change; the new source is added beside it, not inside it
parseJson has 2 direct callers (knownTraps, impact) — a sibling parseJsonl() was added rather than modifying parseJson, leaving both callers undisturbed
The root-level track-3-agent-session.jsonl was a duplicate of test/fixtures/ copy — deleted before commit to avoid the exact drift the product detects
evidence/README.md appeared as a depth-1 caller of adjudicate in graph output — prose matching a symbol name, not a code call site; requires manual verification

code.finding: verify() is the sole direct caller of changedSince; new session evidence is wired here beside the git adapter, not inside it
parseJsonl() added as a sibling to parseJson(); regex literal for line splitting must be written as a RegExp constructor or escape-safe literal to avoid shell/heredoc interpretation issues
Format detection sniffs discriminator field: integer 'type' → entire-protocol, string 'event' → acme-events; ambiguous or absent discriminator goes to degraded[], never guessed
AcmeCode 1.4.2 format: string-tagged envelope with 10 event kinds, file_changed streamed per edit with change: modified|created|deleted, checkpoint_created carries open_questions[]
Original entire-protocol format: integer EventJSON.type enum, AgentSessionJSON with batch modified_files[]/new_files[]/deleted_files[], plus tool_input.file_path on tool events

Three new finding classes: out_of_bounds_by_claim (FAIL), unverified_claims (WARN), unclaimed_changes (WARN); evidence_basis field: deterministic|reconciled|claimed_only; claimed_only is floored at WARN, can never be PASS
No-session verify gains exactly one 'EVIDENCE BASIS' line — described as behaviourally unchanged but not byte-identical; the 'byte-identical' claim was an overclaim that was corrected

workflow: TDD discipline enforced strictly: loadSession was written before its test, caught, deleted, then test-driven from scratch — documented in DESIGN.md §17.3 rather than quietly fixed
A doc comment containing agents/*/internal/... closed a block comment early in TypeScript, causing a parse error — agent protocol path patterns must be in line comments or escaped in block comments

Heredoc injection of multi-line content into bash via Bash tool is unreliable for complex content; Write to a scratchpad file then apply via a Python patch script was the reliable pattern used throughout
Graph impact runs produce evidence artifacts (JSON) that should be saved to evidence/ immediately — they are referenced by judges and the card scores their pre-edit capture
Fixture design: a single fixture mixing both format discriminators (string event + integer type:99) is ambiguous by the detection rule and correctly refused — split into per-format fixtures instead
Entire checkpoint titles come from the user prompt text, not commit messages — commit message bodies (shown by entire checkpoint explain --full) carry the real substance
MCP server smoke test via stdio handshake (initialize → capabilities) should be run after wiring changes to verify no stdout pollution was introduced

friction: Heredoc syntax for multi-line content in bash tool calls consistently failed — had to adopt a Write-to-scratchpad + apply-via-Python-script pattern as a workaround
A doc comment path pattern (agents/*/internal/protocol/types.go) closed a TypeScript block comment prematurely, causing a parse error mid-implementation
DESIGN.md being gitignored was discovered only after writing §16 — required restructuring the submission to make BUILDATHON.md and evidence/ self-contained
graph impact output listed evidence/README.md as a depth-1 caller of adjudicate due to prose matching the symbol name — required manual source verification to distinguish from real call sites
The mixed-format unknown-events fixture (intended by §16 plan) was impossible to implement because the detection rule correctly refused it — required splitting into two fixtures and updating the plan
open_items: BUILDATHON.md checkpoint table rows 3 and 4 still say 'pending' — IDs only exist after commit and need to be backfilled

The claimed_only evidence_basis floor (cannot be PASS) is enforced by type and property test but the live demo path exercises it against a repo-mismatch scenario, not a clean in-repo scenario — a cleaner demo contract would make the safety claim easier to demonstrate to judges
Entire session checkpoint IDs for 'Response to the Curveball' and 'Final implementation and verification' need to be linked by ID in the submission with descriptions of what each proves

The duplicate track-3-agent-session.jsonl at repo root was deleted but its origin (judge attachment vs. local copy) was not documented — worth noting in submission that the canonical fixture is test/fixtures/track-3-agent-session.jsonl
82 passing tests do not include an integration test against a real in-repo agent run with a known sha — all session tests use fixtures with repo-mismatch warnings
